from: July book, night 16 (Hezekiah Trusted the Lord)
p1: Hezekiah became king of Judah when he was twenty-five years old. He did what was right in the Lord’s eyes.
Many people prayed to statues called idols instead of the Lord. So Hezekiah broke the idols into pieces.
Long ago, Moses had made a brass snake. Now people burned sweet smoke to it, as if it were an idol. So Hezekiah broke that too.
p2: The scriptures say, “He trusted in the Lord.” Hezekiah held on tight to the Lord and kept His commandments. And the Lord was with him. The Lord he trusted was Jesus.
You can trust Jesus too, like jumping into loving arms. Tonight, hug your pillow tight. Jesus is always there to hold on to.
old: Hezekiah became the king of Judah. He loved Heavenly Father with all his heart. The people had been worshiping pretend gods and idols. Hezekiah said, “We will follow the true God!”
He took away all the idols and false things. He helped the people remember Heavenly Father. Hezekiah trusted God more than any king before him. He held tight to the Lord and obeyed Him.
Because Hezekiah trusted God, Heavenly Father was with him. The Lord helped him and blessed the people. When troubles came, Hezekiah knew where to turn. He always looked to God first.
Trusting Heavenly Father means believing He will help us. It means choosing Him over everything else. When we trust God, He stays close to us. Trusting God is the best choice a heart can make.
